questions.question: What is a critical point of a function $f\colon X\to\mathbb{R}$?
options: A domain point where $f'$ is zero or undefined.
A point outside the domain of $f$.
A point where $f$ is constant on all of $X$.
questions.explanation: A point $x_0\in X$ in the domain is critical when $f'(x_0)=0$ or $f'(x_0)$ is undefined.
questions.source_support: Definition of critical point.
option_explanations: A critical point must lie in the domain $X$; a point outside $X$ is not a point of the function at all.
A zero of $f$ need not be critical; $f(x)=x$ has $f(0)=0$ but $f'(0)=1\neq 0$, so $0$ is not critical.
Global constancy is not required; $f(x)=x^2$ has a critical point at $0$ ($f'(0)=0$) but is not constant on $\mathbb R$.
